trans.en: making you feel embarrassed so that you are not sure what to do or say

syn.cn: 尴尬的;笨拙的;棘手的;不合适的

ex.en: I hoped he would stop asking awkward questions .
ex.zh: 我希望他不要再问令人难堪的问题。

ex.en: There was an awkward moment when she didn't know whether to shake his hand or kiss his cheek.
ex.zh: 她不知道是该跟他握手还是亲他的脸颊,一时很尴尬。

exam.text: It's awkward, and so awkward that some people will panic and say anything.
The crude technique required educated guesses on exposure times, and involved heavy, awkward equipment - several men had to assist in its transportation.

Researchers analysed the frequency and impact of gaps greater than 2 seconds during conversations, including an overview of previous studies which indicate that the fear of awkward silences can be so extreme that people avoid talking to strangers, even though doing so is likely to be an enjoyable experience.
